import pandas as pd

def main():
    # Define source file paths
    source_files = [
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_66/test_0.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_66/test_1.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_66/test_2.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_66/test_3.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_66/test_4.csv"
    ]

    # List to hold dataframes
    dfs = []

    # Load each source CSV into a dataframe
    for file_path in source_files:
        df = pd.read_csv(file_path)
        # Ensure columns are exactly as target schema and types are string
        df = df.astype({
            'Year': str,
            'Category': str,
            'Nominee': str,
            'Movie': str,
            'Winner': str
        })
        dfs.append(df)

    # Concatenate all source dataframes vertically (union)
    combined_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

    # The target schema is ['Year', 'Category', 'Nominee', 'Movie', 'Winner']
    # The source schemas are identical, so no column renaming or reordering needed.
    # Just ensure columns are in the correct order:
    combined_df = combined_df[['Year', 'Category', 'Nominee', 'Movie', 'Winner']]

    # Optional: Remove duplicates if any (not explicitly stated but often useful)
    combined_df = combined_df.drop_duplicates()

    # Save the combined dataframe to the target path
    target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_66/target_multisource_cot.csv"
    combined_df.to_csv(target_path, index=False)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
